0.title: The Lord, the Giver of Life
0.overview:
Many Christians are confident about God the Father and Jesus the Son, but vague about the Holy Spirit. Some think of him as an impersonal force or power. Others associate him mainly with dramatic experiences and argue about which gifts are for today. Yet without the Spirit, no one would ever be born again, understand the Bible, pray, grow in holiness or persevere to the end.

Jesus told his disciples on the night before he died, it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you (John 16:7). That is an extraordinary statement. The disciples had Jesus with them in person, and he said it was better for them to have the Spirit. The Spirit is not a lesser substitute for Christ. He is Christ's presence with his people everywhere and always.

The Spirit's great work is to glorify Christ. He will glorify me, for he will take what is mine and declare it to you (John 16:14). He is like a floodlight, which is not meant to be looked at but to make something else visible. Where the Spirit is truly at work, people are not fascinated by the Spirit but by Jesus.

Six units: (1) Who the Holy Spirit Is; (2) The Spirit Gives Life; (3) The Spirit Within Us; (4) Walking by the Spirit; (5) The Gifts of the Spirit; (6) The Spirit, the Word and Mission. The question of which gifts continue today is handled in Unit 5 with the main views and a verdict.

1.title: Who the Holy Spirit Is
1.overview:
The Spirit is a person. He is not an "it," a force or an energy. Jesus speaks of him as another Helper (John 14:16), one like himself. The Spirit teaches (John 14:26), speaks (Acts 13:2), intercedes (Rom 8:26), decides (1 Cor 12:11) and can be grieved (Eph 4:30). Forces do not grieve. Only persons do. This matters because a force is something we try to use, but a person is someone we relate to.

The Spirit is God. When Ananias lied to the apostles, Peter said, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit, and then, You have not lied to man but to God (Acts 5:3-4). The Spirit has the attributes of God: he is everywhere present (Ps 139:7), knows the depths of God (1 Cor 2:10-11) and is eternal (Heb 9:14). He does the works of God: he was active in creation (Gen 1:2), inspired Scripture (2 Pet 1:21) and gives new life.

The Spirit is one with the Father and the Son. Jesus told his disciples to baptise in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (Matt 28:19). One name, three persons. Paul's blessing joins them in the same way: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all (2 Cor 13:14). The Spirit is not a junior partner. He is fully God, equal with the Father and the Son, to be worshipped and glorified with them.

The Spirit in the Old Testament. The Spirit did not first appear at Pentecost. He hovered over the waters at creation. He came upon judges, kings and prophets to equip them for their tasks. He gave skill to the craftsmen who built the tabernacle (Exod 31:3). David prayed, take not your Holy Spirit from me (Ps 51:11). And the prophets promised a day when God would pour out his Spirit on all his people (Joel 2:28) and put his Spirit within them (Ezek 36:27). That promise was fulfilled at Pentecost.
1.theology:
Proceeding from the Father and the Son: Jesus speaks of the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, whom he himself will send (John 15:26). The Western church has confessed that the Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, since he is called both the Spirit of God and the Spirit of Christ (Rom 8:9).

Old and new: Believers in the Old Testament were regenerated by the Spirit, for no one can be saved without new birth. What is new since Pentecost is the fullness of the Spirit's work: he is poured out on all believers, not only leaders; he dwells in them permanently; and he unites Jew and Gentile in one body.

Worship the Spirit? Scripture rarely records prayers addressed directly to the Spirit, because his role is to bring us to the Father through the Son. Yet since he is God, it is right to worship him, as the church has always done.
1.examples:
Then: When Paul met some disciples in Ephesus, he asked whether they had received the Holy Spirit when they believed. They said, No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit (Acts 19:2). They had been taught only John's baptism. Many Christians today are not much further along. They know the Spirit exists but have little idea who he is or what he does.

Now: A believer has always prayed "Lord, send your power" as if asking for electricity. Learning that the Spirit is a person who loves her, who can be grieved and who prays for her, she begins to think of him as a constant, gentle companion and to ask, "Am I grieving him?"

A simple test: Do you think of the Holy Spirit as "it" or "he"? The difference shapes how you relate to him.

verseByVerse.quote: And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Helper, to be with you forever, even the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. You know him, for he dwells with you and will be in you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus promises another Helper, another of the same kind as himself. Jesus had been their helper for three years; now the Spirit would be. And he would not leave: to be with you forever. The world cannot receive him because it does not know him, but the disciples know him, for he dwells with them and will be in them.

verseByVerse.quote: But Peter said, "Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back for yourself part of the proceeds of the land? While it remained unsold, did it not remain your own? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? Why is it that you have contrived this deed in your heart? You have not lied to man but to God." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Ananias and Sapphira pretended to give the whole price of their land while keeping part. Peter calls this lying to the Holy Spirit, and in the next breath lying to God. The Spirit is not a force that can be fooled. He is God, who sees the heart. The early church learned to take him seriously.

verseByVerse.quote: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul ends his letter with a blessing that has become one of the most familiar in the church. Grace comes through the Lord Jesus Christ, love from God the Father, and fellowship through the Holy Spirit. The Spirit's particular gift is fellowship: sharing in God's life and in each other's.

verseByVerse.quote: And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh. And I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes and be careful to obey my rules. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God promises a heart transplant: a heart of stone replaced by a heart of flesh. Then he promises more: I will put my Spirit within you. The result is obedience: he will cause you to walk in my statutes. What the law could command but not produce, the Spirit produces from within.

1.reflection:
How would you show from Scripture that the Holy Spirit is a person and not a force?

Read John 14:15-26. What does Jesus say the Spirit will do for his disciples?

Why do you think the Spirit is often the "forgotten" person of the Trinity?

What difference would it make to pray, read and serve as someone in whom God himself dwells?

2.title: The Spirit Gives Life
2.overview:
Nicodemus was a respected teacher of Israel, morally serious and religious. Jesus told him, unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God (John 3:3). Nicodemus did not need improvement. He needed a new beginning, and only the Spirit can give it: unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God (John 3:5).

Why new birth is necessary. By nature we are dead in the trespasses and sins (Eph 2:1). A dead person cannot decide to come alive. The natural person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God, for they are folly to him (1 Cor 2:14). Before the Spirit's work, the gospel seems foolish, unnecessary or unwelcome.

How the Spirit gives life. The Spirit works through the word of God (1 Pet 1:23; Jas 1:18). As the gospel is heard, he opens blind eyes and gives a new heart. Like the wind, he is invisible and sovereign: The wind blows where it wishes, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit (John 3:8). We cannot control or predict the Spirit's work, but we can see its effects.

What new birth produces. Faith and repentance are the first signs of new life. A new love for God, a new hatred of sin, a new hunger for his word and a new love for his people follow. Paul calls it a washing: God saved us, not because of works done by us in righteousness, but according to his own mercy, by the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5).

Sealed by the Spirit. When people believe, the Spirit marks them as God's own. In him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is the guarantee of our inheritance (Eph 1:13-14). A seal marks ownership and protects. A guarantee is a down payment, a first instalment that promises the rest. The Spirit in us now is a foretaste of heaven and a pledge that God will finish what he began.
2.theology:
Regeneration comes first: In the Reformed understanding, new birth is not the result of our faith but its cause. God gives life, and the living person believes. This is why salvation is entirely of grace: even our faith is a gift (Eph 2:8). The Grace of God study covers the views and the verdict on this.

"Born of water and the Spirit": Some take "water" in John 3:5 to mean baptism, so that baptism causes new birth. But Jesus rebukes Nicodemus for not understanding this from the Old Testament (John 3:10). The background is Ezekiel 36:25-27, where God promises to sprinkle clean water and give a new spirit. Water and Spirit together describe the Spirit's cleansing and renewing work, which baptism later signifies.

The Spirit and the word together: The Spirit does not usually work apart from the word, and the word does not save apart from the Spirit. That is why we preach the gospel and pray for the Spirit together.
2.examples:
Then: In Philippi, Paul spoke by a river to a group of women. One of them, Lydia, was already a worshipper of God. Luke says, The Lord opened her heart to pay attention to what was said by Paul (Acts 16:14). Paul spoke the word; the Lord opened her heart. That is how conversion happens.

Now: A mother has prayed for years for her adult son, who has heard the gospel many times and shrugs it off. She has tried every argument. Studying John 3, she realises she cannot argue him into new life. Only the Spirit can give it. She keeps speaking, but she prays more than she argues.

A simple test: Can you see signs of new life in yourself: a love for Christ, a hatred of sin, a hunger for God's word? These are the wind's effects.

verseByVerse.quote: Jesus answered him, "Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God." Nicodemus said to him, "How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother's womb and be born?" Jesus answered, "Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. Do not marvel that I said to you, 'You must be born again.' The wind blows where it wishes, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Nicodemus takes Jesus literally and asks how a grown man can be born again. Jesus explains that there are two kinds of birth. Flesh produces flesh; only the Spirit produces spiritual life. Then he compares the Spirit to the wind, free and invisible yet unmistakable in its effects. New birth is God's work, not ours.

verseByVerse.quote: But when the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, not because of works done by us in righteousness, but according to his own mercy, by the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior, so that being justified by his grace we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul describes salvation with the Trinity at work: God our Saviour shows kindness, the Spirit washes and renews, and the Spirit is poured out through Jesus Christ our Savior. And he underlines what salvation is not: not because of works done by us in righteousness. The washing of regeneration is all mercy.

verseByVerse.quote: In him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is the guarantee of our inheritance until we acquire possession of it, to the praise of his glory. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul traces the order: hearing the word, believing, being sealed. The seal is the Spirit himself. And he is a guarantee, a down payment of the full inheritance still to come. Believers already possess the first instalment of heaven. God does not make a down payment on something he does not intend to complete.

verseByVerse.quote: Now we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, that we might understand the things freely given us by God. And we impart this in words not taught by human wisdom but taught by the Spirit, interpreting spiritual truths to those who are spiritual. The natural person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God, for they are folly to him, and he is not able to understand them because they are spiritually discerned. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Why do some people find the gospel compelling and others find it foolish? Paul's answer is the Spirit. Believers have received the Spirit that we might understand the things freely given us by God. The natural person cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned. This is humbling: if we believe, it is because God opened our eyes.

2.reflection:
Why could Nicodemus's religion and morality not save him?

How does John 3:8 encourage you as you pray for unbelieving friends and family?

What does it mean to you that the Spirit is the "guarantee" of your inheritance?

What evidence of new life do you see in yourself? Thank God for it.

3.title: The Spirit Within Us
3.overview:
One of the most astonishing truths of the New Testament is that God himself lives in every believer. Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? (1 Cor 6:19). In the Old Testament, God's presence dwelt in a tent, then a temple. Now he dwells in his people.

Every believer has the Spirit. There are not two classes of Christians, those who have the Spirit and those who do not. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him (Rom 8:9). If you are in Christ, the Spirit is in you, whether you feel it or not.

The Spirit of adoption. For you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons, by whom we cry, "Abba! Father!" (Rom 8:15). The Spirit turns servants into children. He gives believers the instinct to call God "Father," the cry of a child running to a parent.

The Spirit of assurance. The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God (Rom 8:16). This witness is not usually a voice or a vision. It is the Spirit's quiet work of applying God's promises to our hearts, producing trust, love for God and a growing likeness to Christ, so that we know we belong.

The Spirit who prays. Likewise the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know what to pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words (Rom 8:26). When we cannot find words, when grief or confusion leave us silent, the Spirit is praying for us, and always in line with God's will (Rom 8:27).

The Spirit who unites. The same Spirit who lives in each believer lives in all believers, binding them into one body. For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body (1 Cor 12:13). This is why Christians from different nations and backgrounds feel instantly at home with one another. The same Spirit lives in both.
3.theology:
Baptism in the Spirit: the views. Pentecostal and charismatic teaching often describes baptism in the Spirit as a second experience after conversion, usually evidenced by speaking in tongues, which brings power for service. Others hold that every believer is baptised in the Spirit at conversion, and that later experiences are fillings or renewals of the Spirit's work, not a second baptism.

The verdict: Paul says we were all baptized in one Spirit into one body (1 Cor 12:13), addressing a mixed and immature church. Baptism in the Spirit is the Spirit's work of joining us to Christ at conversion. The delays in Acts (Acts 8; Acts 19) mark the gospel crossing new boundaries, Samaria and the Gentile world, under apostolic witness. They are not a pattern for every believer. But the command to be filled with the Spirit (Eph 5:18) is ongoing. We do not seek a second baptism, but we seek to be continually filled.

Can the Spirit leave a believer? No. He is given to be with you forever (John 14:16). David's prayer in Psalm 51:11 reflected the Old Testament pattern, in which the Spirit's anointing for office could be taken away, as it was from Saul.
3.examples:
Then: The church in Corinth had serious problems, including sexual immorality. Paul did not tell them the Spirit had left. He reminded them that he was there: your body is his temple. The presence of the Spirit is not only a comfort but a reason for holiness (1 Cor 6:18-20).

Now: A Christian sits by her husband's hospital bed, too exhausted and frightened to pray. All she can manage is a sigh. She remembers Romans 8:26. Her silence is not empty. The Spirit is praying for her, with groanings too deep for words. She rests in that.

A simple test: When you pray, do you come to God as a servant hoping to be accepted or as a child calling "Father"? The Spirit of adoption makes the second possible.

verseByVerse.quote: You, however, are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him. But if Christ is in you, although the body is dead because of sin, the Spirit is life because of righteousness. If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul is clear: if you belong to Christ, the Spirit dwells in you. And the Spirit who raised Jesus from the dead will one day raise our mortal bodies too. The Spirit within us is both a present life and a future promise. Our bodies may weaken and die, but the Spirit in them guarantees resurrection.

verseByVerse.quote: For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. For you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons, by whom we cry, "Abba! Father!" The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God, and if children, then heirs—heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, provided we suffer with him in order that we may also be glorified with him. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Spirit leads God's children, frees them from slavish fear and gives them the cry "Abba! Father!" Then he witnesses with their spirit that they are children. And children are heirs, heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ. The path to that inheritance runs through suffering with Christ, but it ends in glory with him.

verseByVerse.quote: Likewise the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know what to pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words. And he who searches hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Christians often feel they do not know how to pray, especially in great suffering. Paul says that is normal. The Spirit helps in our weakness, praying for us in ways too deep for words. And he prays according to the will of God. Even our weakest prayers are carried by a perfect intercessor.

verseByVerse.quote: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul writes this in the middle of warnings about sexual sin. The body is not ours to use as we please, because it is the temple of the Holy Spirit. We were bought with a price. The indwelling Spirit makes the body holy ground. That is why what we do with our bodies matters.

3.reflection:
How does it change your view of yourself to know that you are a temple of the Holy Spirit?

Read Romans 8:12-27. List everything the Spirit does for believers in this passage.

How would you answer a Christian who says they need a second baptism in the Spirit?

When have you been unable to pray? How does Romans 8:26 comfort you?

4.title: Walking by the Spirit
4.overview:
The Christian life is a battle. For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh (Gal 5:17). Every believer feels this pull in two directions. The answer is not self-improvement but the Spirit: walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh (Gal 5:16).

The fruit of the Spirit. But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control (Gal 5:22-23). Notice that it is fruit, not fruits. It is one character, the character of Christ, with nine aspects. And it is fruit, not works. Fruit grows. It cannot be manufactured by effort alone, but it can be cultivated by staying close to the vine (John 15:4-5).

The Spirit and holiness. The Spirit gives the desire and the power to put sin to death: if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live (Rom 8:13). He transforms us gradually into Christ's likeness: we all, with unveiled face, beholding the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another (2 Cor 3:18). Holiness is not instant, but it is real.

The Spirit and Scripture. The Spirit who inspired the Bible also opens it to us. Jesus promised that the Spirit will guide you into all the truth (John 16:13). This promise was given first to the apostles, who wrote the New Testament. But the same Spirit now helps believers understand and believe what was written. This is called illumination. It does not add new truth to Scripture; it helps us see and love what is already there.

Be filled with the Spirit. And do not get drunk with wine, for that is debauchery, but be filled with the Spirit (Eph 5:18). Wine controls a person from outside; the Spirit transforms from within. Paul describes what a Spirit-filled life looks like: singing, thankfulness and mutual submission (Eph 5:19-21). It is not first an emotional experience but a life increasingly governed by Christ's word (Col 3:16).

Do not grieve the Spirit. And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God (Eph 4:30). The context is our speech, anger, bitterness and unkindness. The Spirit is grieved by what destroys the unity he creates.
4.theology:
Effort and grace: Walking by the Spirit does not mean passive waiting. Paul commands effort: put to death, put off, put on, strive. But our effort depends on his work. Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling, for it is God who works in you, both to will and to work for his good pleasure (Phil 2:12-13).

Guidance: The Spirit guides believers chiefly through Scripture, wisdom, godly counsel and providence, not through private messages that must be obeyed as if they were God's word. Impressions and feelings should be tested by Scripture and held humbly.

Quenching the Spirit: Paul warns, Do not quench the Spirit (1 Thess 5:19). In context, it concerns despising God's word spoken in the church. We quench the Spirit when we resist his word.
4.examples:
Then: The disciples who fled at Jesus' arrest were the same men who, after Pentecost, stood before the council and refused to stop preaching. The council saw the boldness of Peter and John and recognized that they had been with Jesus (Acts 4:13). The Spirit had changed fearful men into courageous witnesses.

Now: A man with a quick temper has tried for years to control it with willpower. He begins each day reading Scripture and asking the Spirit to produce patience in him. He still fails sometimes. But his wife notices that he apologises faster, and that the outbursts are rarer. The fruit is growing slowly, as fruit does.

A simple test: Which aspect of the fruit of the Spirit is least visible in your life? Ask the Spirit to grow it, and stay close to the vine.

verseByVerse.quote: But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh. For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh, for these are opposed to each other, to keep you from doing the things you want to do. But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. Now the works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, sensuality, idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, fits of anger, rivalries, dissensions, divisions, envy, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these. I warn you, as I warned you before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God. But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law. And those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. If we live by the Spirit, let us also keep in step with the Spirit. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul sets two lists side by side. The works of the flesh are obvious and destructive. The fruit of the Spirit is beautiful and life-giving. Believers have crucified the flesh, yet must still keep in step with the Spirit. The victory has been won at the cross, and we now live it out day by day.

verseByVerse.quote: "I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth, for he will not speak on his own authority, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will declare to you the things that are to come. He will glorify me, for he will take what is mine and declare it to you. All that the Father has is mine; therefore I said that he will take what is mine and declare it to you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus had more to teach than his disciples could bear. The Spirit would complete the teaching, guiding the apostles into all the truth. Notice the Spirit's aim: He will glorify me. The Spirit always points away from himself to Christ. Any teaching that exalts experiences of the Spirit above Christ is not from him.

verseByVerse.quote: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. And we all, with unveiled face, beholding the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another. For this comes from the Lord who is the Spirit. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Moses veiled his face after seeing God's glory. Believers now look at the Lord's glory with unveiled faces, and as they look, they change. Transformation comes through beholding. The more we gaze at Christ in Scripture, the more the Spirit makes us like him, step by step, from one degree of glory to another.

verseByVerse.quote: Let no corrupting talk come out of your mouths, but only such as is good for building up, as fits the occasion, that it may give grace to those who hear. And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption. Let all bitterness and wrath and anger and clamor and slander be put away from you, along with all malice. Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul places the warning about grieving the Spirit between instructions about speech and anger. The Spirit is not grieved only by dramatic sins but by corrupting talk, bitterness and malice. Kindness, tenderness and forgiveness please him, because they reflect what God has done for us in Christ.

4.reflection:
Read Galatians 5:16-26. Where do you see the flesh and the Spirit in conflict in your life?

Why does Paul call it the "fruit" of the Spirit rather than the "works"?

How does 2 Corinthians 3:18 suggest we grow in holiness?

What kind of speech or attitude might be grieving the Spirit in your life?

5.title: The Gifts of the Spirit
5.overview:
The ascended Christ gives gifts to his church through the Spirit. To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good (1 Cor 12:7). Every believer has at least one gift, and every gift is meant to serve others, not to impress them.

Many gifts, one body. The New Testament lists many gifts: teaching, serving, encouraging, giving, leading, showing mercy, administration, helping, evangelism, faith, wisdom and others (Rom 12:6-8; 1 Cor 12:8-10, 28; Eph 4:11; 1 Pet 4:10-11). Paul compares the church to a body. The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you." Every member is needed, and the weaker members are indispensable (1 Cor 12:21-22).

Gifts are for serving. As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace (1 Pet 4:10). Gifts are not trophies but tools. They are given by grace, so no one can boast; they are given to all, so no one can opt out.

Love is greater. Between his two chapters on gifts, Paul places 1 Corinthians 13. The Corinthians were proud of their spectacular gifts but lacking in love. Paul says that tongues without love are a noisy gong, and prophetic powers without love are nothing. The most important evidence of the Spirit is not a spectacular gift but love.

How to find your gift. Rather than taking long inventories, the best way is usually to serve where there is need, and to listen to what mature believers see in you. Gifts are discovered in use. And faithfulness in small tasks matters more than identifying the perfect role.
5.theology:
Do the miraculous gifts continue? The views. Continuationists hold that all the gifts of the New Testament, including prophecy, tongues and healing, continue today. Many read 1 Corinthians 13:10 (when the perfect comes, the partial will pass away) as referring to Christ's return. Some hold an "open but cautious" position. Cessationists hold that the gifts tied to giving new revelation and confirming the apostles' message ceased when the apostolic foundation was complete, while the ordinary gifts continue.

The verdict: The cessationist view is the most faithful to the New Testament's own shape, and it does not rest on 1 Corinthians 13:10, which most likely refers to Christ's return. The church is built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets (Eph 2:20), and a foundation is laid once. The miraculous signs confirmed the apostles' message (Heb 2:3-4) and are called the signs of a true apostle (2 Cor 12:12). The faith has been once for all delivered to the saints (Jude 3), and Scripture is sufficient (2 Tim 3:16-17). Prophecy that claims to speak God's words today would add to Scripture.

What this does not mean: God still does miracles when he chooses, and he heals in answer to prayer (Jas 5:14-15). Missionaries have seen remarkable providences. The Spirit is not less active today. Cessationism is about the gifts that gave new revelation, not about God's power. And believers who hold the continuationist view are brothers and sisters, many of them deeply godly.
5.examples:
Then: The church in Corinth was not lacking in any gift (1 Cor 1:7), yet it was divided, proud and immoral. Spectacular gifts did not make it a spiritual church. The Thessalonians, by contrast, were known for their work of faith and labor of love and steadfastness of hope (1 Thess 1:3).

Now: A retired man assumes he has no spiritual gift because he cannot preach or lead. But he notices lonely people after the service and phones the sick every week. The elders see what he does not: he has a gift of mercy and encouragement, and the church would be poorer without him.

A simple test: How are you using your gifts to serve others in your church? If you do not know your gift, where is there a need you could start meeting?

verseByVerse.quote: Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are varieties of service, but the same Lord; and there are varieties of activities, but it is the same God who empowers them all in everyone. To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good. For to one is given through the Spirit the utterance of wisdom, and to another the utterance of knowledge according to the same Spirit, to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another the ability to distinguish between spirits, to another various kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues. All these are empowered by one and the same Spirit, who apportions to each one individually as he wills. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul emphasises unity in variety. Different gifts, but the same Spirit; different service, but the same Lord; different activities, but the same God. The Trinity is the pattern of the church: unity without uniformity. And the Spirit distributes gifts as he wills. We do not choose our gifts; we receive them.

verseByVerse.quote: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal. And if I have prophetic powers, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. If I give away all I have, and if I deliver up my body to be burned, but have not love, I gain nothing. Love is patient and kind; love does not envy or boast; it is not arrogant or rude. It does not insist on its own way; it is not irritable or resentful; it does not rejoice at wrongdoing, but rejoices with the truth. Love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul says that without love, the greatest gifts are worthless. Then he describes love by what it does: it is patient and kind; it does not envy, boast or insist on its own way. These are not abstract virtues but marks of a person. They describe Christ himself, and they are the true sign of the Spirit's presence.

verseByVerse.quote: So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God, built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the cornerstone, in whom the whole structure, being joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord. In him you also are being built together into a dwelling place for God by the Spirit. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The church is God's household, a temple growing on a foundation. The apostles and prophets are the foundation, and Christ is the cornerstone. A foundation is laid once and then built upon. This is the main reason to believe that the apostolic and prophetic gifts that gave new revelation belonged to the founding era of the church.

verseByVerse.quote: As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace: whoever speaks, as one who speaks oracles of God; whoever serves, as one who serves by the strength that God supplies—in order that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ. To him belong glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter divides gifts into two broad groups: speaking and serving. Whoever speaks should speak as one who speaks oracles of God, faithfully handling his word. Whoever serves should serve by the strength God supplies. Either way, the goal is the same: in order that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ.

5.reflection:
What gifts has God given you? How do you know? Ask someone who knows you well.

Why does Paul place 1 Corinthians 13 between chapters 12 and 14?

Summarise in your own words the cessationist and continuationist views. Which arguments seem strongest to you?

How can you serve someone in your church this week with the gift God has given you?

6.title: The Spirit, the Word and Mission
6.overview:
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth (Acts 1:8). The Spirit is given for mission. His power is not for private enjoyment but for public witness.

Pentecost. Fifty days after Passover, the disciples were gathered in Jerusalem. A sound like a mighty wind filled the house, tongues as of fire rested on each one, and they began to speak in other languages, declaring the mighty works of God to pilgrims from every nation (Acts 2:1-11). At Babel, God confused languages and scattered the nations. At Pentecost, he began to gather them through the gospel. Peter preached Christ crucified and risen, and three thousand were baptised that day.

The Spirit convicts the world. Jesus said the Spirit will convict the world concerning sin and righteousness and judgment (John 16:8). We cannot convince anyone of their sin or of Christ's worth. The Spirit can. This takes the pressure off evangelism. Our job is to speak faithfully; his is to open hearts.

The Spirit and the word. The Spirit's chief instrument is the word of God. Paul calls Scripture the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God (Eph 6:17). The Spirit inspired it, illuminates it and uses it to convict and convert. We should never set the Spirit against the word, as if being "led by the Spirit" meant going beyond Scripture. Where the word is faithfully preached, the Spirit is at work.

The Spirit gives boldness. When the early church faced threats, they prayed, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and continued to speak the word of God with boldness (Acts 4:31). They did not ask for safety but for courage. Believers who feel timid about sharing their faith should pray for the same thing.
6.theology:
Pentecost is unrepeatable and ongoing: Pentecost was a once-for-all event in the history of salvation, like the cross and resurrection. The Spirit was poured out on the church, and he has never been withdrawn. We do not need another Pentecost. We need to rely on the Spirit already given.

Tongues at Pentecost: The tongues at Pentecost were real human languages, understood by the hearers (Acts 2:6-8). They were a sign that the gospel was for all nations.

Prayer for the Spirit: Jesus said, how much more will the heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him! (Luke 11:13). Believers have the Spirit, yet we should pray for more of his work in us, in our churches and in our world.
6.examples:
Then: Peter, who had denied Jesus before a servant girl, preached to thousands in the same city weeks later. He spoke of Jesus whom you crucified (Acts 2:36). The hearers were cut to the heart (Acts 2:37). The same man, the same city, but now filled with the Spirit.

Now: A shy woman has never spoken to her neighbours about Christ. She begins praying each morning for boldness and for opportunities. A few weeks later, a neighbour mentions a hospital diagnosis. She offers to pray and finds herself explaining why she trusts God. She did not feel brave. She simply asked, and spoke.

A simple test: When did you last pray specifically for the Spirit to give you boldness to speak about Christ?

verseByVerse.quote: So when they had come together, they asked him, "Lord, will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?" He said to them, "It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by his own authority. But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The disciples asked about the timing of the kingdom. Jesus redirects them: the times are the Father's business; their business is witness. And the Spirit will give them power for it. The circles of mission widen from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth, and the rest of Acts follows that map.

verseByVerse.quote: When the day of Pentecost arrived, they were all together in one place. And suddenly there came from heaven a sound like a mighty rushing wind, and it filled the entire house where they were sitting. And divided tongues as of fire appeared to them and rested on each one of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The signs of Pentecost echo the Old Testament: a rushing wind, like the breath that brought the dry bones to life (Ezek 37:9-10), and fire, as at Sinai. Now the fire rests not on a mountain but on each believer. And the first thing the Spirit does is give speech: the disciples declare God's mighty works. The Spirit's coming is immediately a missionary event.

verseByVerse.quote: Nevertheless, I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you. And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and righteousness and judgment: concerning sin, because they do not believe in me; concerning righteousness, because I go to the Father, and you will see me no longer; concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world is judged. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus explains why his leaving is to the disciples' advantage: the Spirit will come and convict the world. He will show people their sin of unbelief, Christ's righteousness vindicated by his return to the Father, and the judgment of Satan already passed. Evangelism depends on this work of the Spirit.

verseByVerse.quote: And now, Lord, look upon their threats and grant to your servants to continue to speak your word with all boldness, while you stretch out your hand to heal, and signs and wonders are performed through the name of your holy servant Jesus." And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and continued to speak the word of God with boldness. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Under threat from the authorities, the church prayed. They did not ask God to remove the danger. They asked for boldness to keep speaking his word. God answered by filling them with the Spirit. The place shook, but the main result was not the shaking. It was that they continued to speak the word of God with boldness.

6.reflection:
Read Acts 2:1-41. What does the Spirit do, and what is the result?

How does John 16:8 take pressure off you in sharing your faith?

Why is it dangerous to set being "led by the Spirit" against Scripture?

Who in your life do you want to hear the gospel? Pray for boldness and for the Spirit to open their heart.
